Enterprise MCP Essentials›Tune the Tool Contract

Fix the contract, not the prompt

Intermediate 45 minutes Lab 3 of 3
Introduction

In this lab, you'll act as integration engineer for IDEA Brands — hardening the tools behind Maya's AI client so it pauses on ambiguous data and speaks plainly when a search comes back empty. The lab data is synthetic and intentionally messy.

MO
Maya Okonkwo
Tier-1 Support Agent · IDEA Brands

She asked about Nexus Solutions. The assistant picked a Nexus Solutions — in the wrong region — and acted on it.

The question

When the model picks wrong, what do you change — the prompt or the tool?

You'll learn how to

  • Turn two observed failures into durable tool-level fixes

What you'll need

  • The multi-system Customer Support Hub from Lab 2, connected to LibreChat
  • Familiarity with reading and editing a Workato recipe (Foundations 1 or equivalent) — you'll stop a recipe, add an If/Else branch, and restart it
Phase 1

Tune the tool contract

In this phase, you'll turn two observed failures into durable tool-level fixes.

Pattern

Tool design as a contract

Names and descriptions are the model's first signal for tool selection; the input/output schema is the second. When behavior is wrong, fix the contract, not the prompt: add ambiguity gates to descriptions, and make tools return structured, informative results — even when the result is empty.

1.1

Make the model ask before it acts

The synthetic data has duplicate account names across regions — "Nexus Solutions" exists in more than one geography. Ask about one and the model may pick a match and act on it without checking. The fix isn't a better prompt; it's a better tool description.

Overview

Edit the search_accounts tool description to add an explicit ambiguity gate: when more than one account matches, present the matches and require confirmation before any further tool runs. Then reconnect the server in LibreChat and re-test with a duplicate name.

Heads up

Fix the contract, not the prompt

It's tempting to coach the model in chat ("always confirm first"). That fix lives in one conversation and evaporates on the next. Putting the gate in the tool description makes it a property of the tool — every client, every conversation, every time.

Apply these values
FieldValue
Toolsearch_accounts
Add to descriptionAn ambiguity gate + confirmation requirement
ThenReconnect the server in LibreChat
Detailed steps 6 steps

The duplicate-name problem is a tool-design problem, not a prompting one. You'll bake a confirmation gate into the search_accounts description so the model pauses on ambiguous matches, then reconnect so LibreChat picks it up.

  • In LibreChat, ask about a duplicate-named account — the data seeds several across geographies: Nexus Solutions, Titan Technologies, Matrix Solutions, Spectrum Technologies — and watch the model pick one match and act on it without asking. That's the behavior you're about to fix.
  • In your server's Tools section, find search_accounts and edit its description.
  • Add: When more than one account matches, do not perform any additional action until the person in chat explicitly confirms which account to use. If multiple matches are found, present the matches and ask them to choose one.
  • Save the description.
  • In LibreChat, open MCP Settings, find YourName MCP, and reconnect it, then start a new chat.
  • Re-ask about Nexus Solutions and confirm the model now pauses for your choice.
Verify a duplicate-name query makes LibreChat present the matches and wait for you to pick one, instead of acting on a guess.
1.2

Make empty results speak

Not every failure is a crash. A search for a nonexistent customer returns an empty list — and if the tool says nothing, the model can't tell an empty result from an error or a timeout. Make the tool speak even when it finds nothing.

Overview

First, ask LibreChat for info about a made-up customer like FooBarDewey and watch the unhelpful behavior. Then edit the search_accounts recipe: after the search step, branch on whether the result list size equals zero. On the empty path, return a clear structured message; on the else path, return the results as before.

Apply these values
FieldValue
Recipesearch_accounts (stop before editing)
BranchIf list size equals 0
If (yes)Return: Search completed successfully. No accounts matched the provided criteria. Ask for clarification.
Else (no)Move the existing return into this path

The empty-result contract. The search runs, then an If/Else reads the list size: size = 0 returns a structured "no accounts matched" message; otherwise the existing return passes the results through.

Detailed steps 8 steps

An empty result is still a result. You'll branch the search_accounts recipe on the search's list size so it returns an honest "nothing matched" message instead of the silence the model otherwise has to guess at.

  • In LibreChat, ask for all account info about a non-existent customer such as FooBarDewey and observe the empty, unhelpful response.
  • In Workato, locate the search_accounts recipe and stop it — a running recipe is locked against edits — then click Edit.
  • Below step 2 (the search), add If / Else conditional steps.
  • Set the If condition to check whether the result list size equals 0.
  • In the If (yes) branch, add a Return data from a recipe function action. In Account details, return: Search completed successfully. No accounts matched the provided criteria. Ask for clarification.
  • In the No / Else branch, drag the existing return into the indented path.
  • Save the recipe, then restart it. (Recipe functions can be tested by repeating jobs from the job history.)
  • Return to LibreChat, start a new chat, and re-ask about FooBarDewey.
Verify asking about a non-existent customer returns your Search completed successfully. No accounts matched the provided criteria. Ask for clarification. message — check the search_accounts job report if you want the proof. LibreChat will typically follow up with a clarifying question instead of stalling.

Reflect

Now that both fixes live in the tools, consider what that buys you beyond this workshop.

  • You fixed the duplicate-account problem in the tool description rather than in the chat. What does that buy you across many users and conversations?
  • An empty search result and a service error look the same to a model that gets silence. Why is distinguishing them worth a recipe branch?
  • The ambiguity gate lives in one tool's description. What would change — for better and worse — if you pushed the same rule up into the server instructions instead?

Wrap-up

The next time Maya asks about Nexus Solutions, the assistant lists the matches and waits. When a customer doesn't exist, it says so and asks a better question. Neither behavior depends on how anyone phrases the prompt — the tools she relies on carry the rules now.

Patterns to carry forward:

  • Fix the contract, not the prompt. Ambiguity gates and structured returns live in the tool and outlast any single conversation.
  • Tools must speak on every outcome. Empty and error are results too — return them plainly so the model can decide what to do next.
  • Reconnect after every server change. The client caches the server's surface; the re-fetch is what makes your fix real in chat.

Bonus challenges

Still have time? Push the contract further.

  • You added an ambiguity gate to search_accounts. Find another tool that acts on a guess and give it the same confirmation requirement.
  • Add monitor steps to the search_accounts recipe to handle errors, and add discrete return details for when duplicate accounts are found.
